task.description: Design lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md: Letflow.Definitions.rollback_definition_version/4, porting R-Co's src/definition/rollback.zig (PRM-08) onto REQ-027's process_definitions and REQ-035/037's promotion_reviews tables -- permission guard (injectable, no default, checked before any row read/locked), single serializable transaction for the FOR UPDATE lock + guard cases + version-pointer swap, event append via an injectable event_appender (no working EventStore.append/2 path exists yet for a non-instance-scoped event), and promotion_reviews supersession. No implementation code -- signatures, @specs, algorithm-as-pseudocode, invariants, open questions only.
acceptance_criteria: Every REQ-038 acceptance criterion (5, docs/requirements.yaml) maps to a concrete design element -- no TBD
Function signature, @spec, error union, and both injectable-opt shapes fully specified
DB reads/writes (tables, columns, lock/guard mechanics) fully described -- no migration, no schema change
Open questions listed explicitly, not silently resolved -- especially anywhere REQ-036/037's established precedent doesn't fit REQ-038's specific case cleanly
No implementation code (.ex code blocks) present anywhere in the design doc

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md. Placed rollback_definition_version/4 directly in lib/letflow/definitions.ex (matching the requirement's literal target name, unlike Promotion/PromotionReviewStore's separate-submodule shape). Reused promotion.ex's exact injectable permission_checker/event_appender shapes (both Keyword.fetch!/2'd, no built-in default) -- independently re-confirmed against event_store.ex directly that platform_instance_id/0 still doesn't resolve to a real instance_projections row, so a hardcoded EventStore.append/2 call would deterministically fail here too, same as promotion.ex's own disclosed gap. Surfaced three load-bearing findings not obvious from requirements.yaml's R-Co-derived prose, each documented with its own section and flagged as an open question where unresolved: (1) process_definitions.status has no :superseded value in Letflow's shipped 4-value enum (draft/active/deprecated/archived) -- this design maps R-Co's SUPERSEDED onto :deprecated, the same value promote_definition/3 already reuses for automatic supersession, with a stated soundness argument (PD-04's transition table makes :deprecated only reachable via :active); (2) process_definitions.version is a free-form string (e.g. "3.0.0"), not R-Co's u32, so target_version/rolled_back_from_version are String.t() throughout; (3) promotion_reviews.def_id stores process_key (a string), not a definition UUID, so REQ-038's lookup can only scope to the process_key as a whole, not the specific former-active version -- flagged as OQ-5 with a stated, non-silent resolution. Also flagged and concretely resolved (not left TBD): PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3's allowed_source_statuses currently excludes :approved (only [:applied, :failed, :rejected]), but AC4 requires superseding applied OR approved rows -- this design proposes a small, explicit widening to that already-merged module (adding :approved), called out for REVIEWER sign-off since it changes that module's own stated 'exactly 7 permitted edges' invariant. Also flagged a pre-existing index-predicate mismatch discovered while reading REQ-035's shipped migration: idx_promotion_review_rollback_lookup's WHERE predicate is status IN ('applied','superseded'), not ('applied','approved') as REQ-038 actually needs -- not a correctness gap (Postgres still returns correct rows without full index coverage) so not blocking, cited in Sources Read §0 rather than as a numbered open question. Deliberately diverged from R-Co's literal 'single serialisable transaction encompassing swap+event+supersede' framing (flagged as OQ-3, MAJOR): the version-pointer swap runs in its own transaction that commits before the injected event_appender is ever called, mirroring promote_definition/3's own already-REVIEWER-approved precedent of never nesting an opaque injected closure inside a transaction this function itself owns. No implementation code included anywhere in the document.

issues.description: OQ-3 in the design doc: this design places the event-append and promotion_reviews-supersede steps AFTER the version-pointer-swap transaction commits, diverging from R-Co's own PRM-08 design doc ('a single serialisable transaction'). Forced by opts[:event_appender]'s opaque transactionality, matching promote_definition/3's own precedent -- REVIEWER should confirm this tradeoff is still accepted for REQ-038 or reopen both together.

OQ-5 in the design doc: promotion_reviews.def_id stores process_key, not a definition-scoped id, so REQ-038's supersede-lookup cannot be scoped to the specific former-active version -- only to the process_key as a whole. No DB constraint rules out more than one applied/approved row matching at once. This design supersedes every match but names only the most-recently-inserted one as the singular superseded_review_id return field. Flagged for REVIEWER; a real fix would need a schema change out of REQ-038's own scope.

§7 of the design doc proposes widening PromotionReviewStore.supersede_review/3's allowed_source_statuses from [:applied, :failed, :rejected] to include :approved, a change to an already-merged, gate-approved module (REQ-037) whose moduledoc currently states 'exactly 7 permitted edges, no 8th possible.' Concretely specified (not TBD) but requires REVIEWER sign-off before ELIXIR-DEV implements it, per core-directives.md's 'don't silently re-decide what a decision record already settled.'

REQ-035's shipped migration index idx_promotion_review_rollback_lookup (built explicitly 'for PRM-08 rollback's superseded-lookup queries') has predicate status IN ('applied','superseded'), not ('applied','approved') as REQ-038's own lookup actually filters on. Not a correctness gap -- Postgres still returns correct rows for the 'approved' branch via a non-index-covered scan -- but the index as built doesn't fully cover the query it was purpose-built for. Worth a follow-up migration correcting the predicate; out of REQ-038's own scope to fix (REQ-035 is already done/merged).
